description: The hub's AI Failures register: source-linked cases where a company's AI went wrong in public (chatbots promising refunds that did not exist, biased screening, unchecked generated content, agents with too much access, rollouts reversed), each with what went wrong, the company's response, the outcome (fixed, paused, ended, ruling, settlement) and the lesson, grouped into failure patterns with 'how to avoid' steps. Filter by topic, company (as deployer or vendor), pattern, industry or outcome; with no arguments it lists the newest cases and every pattern. Use it for 'what can go wrong with X?', 'has Y had AI failures?' or risk checks before a rollout. Each case has its sources and HubUrl (its page on aiusecasehub.com).

company.description: Only cases involving this company, as the one running the system or as its vendor.

industry.description: Only cases in this industry, for example Retail, Finance or Public Sector.

limit.description: Maximum cases. Public previews return at most 3; personal-key access permits up to 20.

outcome.description: One of: fixed, paused, ended, ruling, settlement, running.

pattern.description: A failure pattern slug or name from a previous result, for example 'agent-with-too-much-access'.

query.description: Optional topic in a few words, for example 'customer chatbot refunds' or 'hiring bias'.

security.description: true for security incidents only, false to leave them out.

name: search_ai_failures
title: Search documented enterprise AI failures
